insights.insight: $5M in cryptographically verified purchase GMV has cleared across 95,730 receipts — a deterministic commerce signal base that probabilistic cookie targeting cannot replicate at any price.

Structural daily intake runs 340–370 verified receipts per day with a confirmed UTC rollover burst pattern across seven consecutive cycles, indicating a stable and predictable signal supply rather than spiky promotional inflows.

Grocery-supermarkets leads by receipt count (1,376 over 14 days, $61,816 GMV) while retail-department-stores leads on implied spend-per-receipt — giving media buyers two distinct audience segments from the same verified dataset.

Walmart (355 receipts), Costco (165), Kroger (156), Safeway (139), and Aldi (129) are the top verified purchaser pools over 14 days — confirmed buyers, not modeled lookalikes, usable for competitive conquest or loyalty targeting.

Verified purchase signals now span 20 confirmed metro areas, with the 17→19→20 progression occurring within three days — coverage is expanding, though the most recent claimed 21st metro has not yet confirmed as structural.

Dollar-denominated value per verified receipt holds at approximately $0.10, establishing a concrete floor for what cryptographic purchase proof costs relative to the $5+ CPM brands routinely pay for probabilistic inference.
